name: Nancy Kerrigan
positive_description: Won the U.S. Figure Skating Championships ladies' title.
negative_description: Finished second at the Lillehammer Olympics, narrowly losing the gold medal to Oksana Baiul.
notes: National championship title versus explicit Olympic runner-up loss.

name: Fran Tarkenton
positive_description: Won the NFC Championship with the Minnesota Vikings, earning a Super Bowl berth.
negative_description: Lost Super Bowl XI with the Minnesota Vikings to the Oakland Raiders.
notes: Distinct-year major postseason win/loss; calendar-year labeling.

name: Wade Boggs
positive_description: Won the World Series with the New York Yankees.
negative_description: The Yankees lost the AL Division Series to Seattle after taking a 2-0 series lead.
notes: MLB source discusses the 1995 postseason loss and 1996 World Series title.

name: Linda Ronstadt
positive_description: The Broadway revival of The Pirates of Penzance became an award-winning hit; Ronstadt was Tony-nominated.
negative_description: The film adaptation of The Pirates of Penzance performed poorly theatrically; AFI records only $694,497 in its first three weeks.
notes: Stage project success versus film adaptation commercial failure.

name: Annie Lennox
positive_description: Eurythmics broke through internationally with Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This), including a U.S. No. 1 single.
negative_description: Eurythmics' debut album In the Garden failed to gain meaningful chart traction.
notes: Discrete album underperformance versus later breakthrough project.

name: Dennis Hopper
positive_description: Easy Rider became a major breakthrough and highly successful film project.
negative_description: The Last Movie failed on release and fell into distribution limbo.
notes: Same BFI retrospective explicitly contrasts the breakthrough with the later failure.

name: Meat Loaf
positive_description: Released Bat Out of Hell, which became one of the best-selling albums of all time.
negative_description: Midnight at the Lost and Found was a critical failure and sold poorly.
notes: Album-level success versus explicitly described album failure.

name: Jerry Lee Lewis
positive_description: Another Place, Another Time became a No. 4 country hit and launched Lewis's major country comeback.
negative_description: Country Songs for City Folks failed to find an audience during Lewis's low-traction Smash Records period.
notes: Discrete 1965 album underperformance versus 1968 hit/comeback project.

name: Laurence Olivier
positive_description: Hamlet won the Academy Award for Best Picture and Olivier won Best Actor.
negative_description: Richard III failed at the box office and did not recoup its costs.
notes: Film-project success versus explicitly documented box-office failure.

name: Dianne Feinstein
positive_description: Won election to the United States Senate from California.
negative_description: Lost the California gubernatorial election.
notes: U.S. House Historian profile records both electoral outcomes.

name: Lee Iacocca
positive_description: Was elected chairman of Chrysler.
negative_description: Was forced out as president of Ford.
notes: Explicit executive role gain versus forced role loss.

name: Mario Monti
positive_description: Was appointed President of the Council of Ministers of Italy.
negative_description: His centrist coalition underperformed in the 2013 general election, receiving about 10.5% in the Chamber vote.
notes: Official appointment versus explicit electoral defeat/underperformance.

name: Rick Perry
positive_description: Won election as Governor of Texas in his own right.
negative_description: Dropped out of the Republican presidential nomination race after his campaign collapsed.
notes: Statewide election win versus failed presidential nomination bid.

name: Julio María Sanguinetti
positive_description: Was elected President of Uruguay for a second term.
negative_description: Lost the Colorado Party presidential primary to Ernesto Talvi.
notes: Presidential election win versus explicit party-primary defeat.

name: Enrico Letta
positive_description: Became Prime Minister of Italy.
negative_description: Resigned after Matteo Renzi's party move withdrew the political support sustaining his government.
notes: Political support withdrawal is treated as explicit role loss, not a routine term end.

name: Iain Duncan Smith
positive_description: Became Leader of the Conservative Party.
negative_description: Lost a Conservative parliamentary confidence vote and was forced out as party leader.
notes: Explicit party leadership gain versus confidence-vote removal.

name: Jean Charest
positive_description: Led the Quebec Liberal Party to a majority and became Premier of Quebec.
negative_description: Lost his own seat as his government was defeated in the Quebec election.
notes: Same biography records both the 2003 win and 2012 defeat.

name: Kurt Georg Kiesinger
positive_description: Was elected Federal Chancellor of West Germany.
negative_description: The 1969 federal election ended the CDU/CSU-led government and Kiesinger lost the chancellorship.
notes: Official Federal Chancellor history supports both events.

name: José Sócrates
positive_description: Led Portugal's Socialist Party to an absolute-majority election victory and became Prime Minister.
negative_description: Resigned after parliament rejected his government's austerity/stability program.
notes: Election victory versus parliamentary defeat that directly triggered resignation.

name: Mario Soares
positive_description: Was elected President of Portugal.
negative_description: Lost the Portuguese presidential election, finishing well behind the winner.
notes: Presidential election win versus later presidential election loss.

name: Nicolae Ceaușescu
positive_description: Succeeded Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej as leader of Romania's Communist Party.
negative_description: Was overthrown during the Romanian Revolution and lost power.
notes: Explicit leadership accession versus overthrow.

name: Steve Jobs
positive_description: Returned to lead Apple and took over as chief executive.
negative_description: Was pushed out of Apple's management after losing an internal power struggle.
notes: One AP retrospective documents both ouster and return to leadership.

name: Peter Ueberroth
positive_description: Was elected Commissioner of Major League Baseball.
negative_description: Ended his California gubernatorial campaign, publicly acknowledging he had lost.
notes: Major executive appointment versus explicit failed gubernatorial bid.

name: Wilfried Martens
positive_description: Became Prime Minister of Belgium.
negative_description: Was ousted from the premiership after the 1991 election.
notes: European Parliament historical archive explicitly describes the 1991 ouster.

name: Michael Bloomberg
positive_description: Was elected Mayor of New York City.
negative_description: Suspended his presidential campaign after poor Super Tuesday results.
notes: Mayoral election win versus failed presidential nomination campaign.

name: Franz Josef Strauss
positive_description: Became Minister-President of Bavaria.
negative_description: Failed in his campaign to become Chancellor of West Germany.
notes: State leadership gain versus explicit federal chancellorship election defeat.

name: Alberto Fujimori
positive_description: Won Peru's presidential election and took office.
negative_description: Peru's Congress rejected his resignation and removed him from the presidency.
notes: Presidential election win versus explicit congressional removal.

name: Rahul Gandhi
positive_description: Won the Rae Bareli parliamentary seat in India's general election.
negative_description: Lost the Amethi parliamentary seat in India's general election.
notes: Explicit parliamentary election win versus loss.
